chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a rope made from pig hair by which water is drawn from the well: may wudu (ablution) be performed from that water? He said: “There is no harm.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report is understood to mean when the hair does not reach the water, because if it were to reach it, it would corrupt it, as we have explained in the Book of Hunting and Slaughtered Animals.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water is taken
key_terms.الْحَبْلِ: the rope used to draw water
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water being drawn from the well
key_terms.شَعْرِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pig hair, discussed here in relation to impurity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.مُفْسِدًا: causing corruption or invalidation of the water
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution) with the water

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with well-water drawn by a rope made from pig hair?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of using well-water drawn by a rope made from pig hair for wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام permits it, while Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that this is to be understood in the case where the pig hair itself does not come into contact with the water.
